title: MF vs PMS vs AIF
blurb: Mutual funds, PMS and AIFs compared on ticket, ownership, liquidity, cost, tax and regulation — and which client fits each.

rows: New employees (all sections), sales team (talk-tracks, role-plays, niche topics); investors as awareness material
About 78 minutes of lessons, plus role-play and the final quiz
Each L.E.A.R.N. stage has: what to know, how to do it, a talk-track, and the investor takeaway

sources: SEBI Master Circular for Mutual Funds (current edition)
NISM Series XIX-A (AIF Categories I & II) and XIX-B (Category III) workbooks

cards.q: Maximum investors in an AIF scheme
a: 1,000 investors per scheme.
Only by private placement, through SEBI-registered intermediaries. No public advertising or mass marketing.
MF: V-A. PMS: XXI-A. AIF: XIX-A (Category I & II) and XIX-B (Category III).
Category III: trail only. Category I & II: up to one-third upfront, the rest as trail over the tenure.
Foundation → mutual fund core → PMS → AIF. Each rung sits on the one below; it never replaces it.
In PE/VC AIFs, early years often show low or negative returns (fees and investing first); gains, if any, come later as investments are exited.
The manager's share of an AIF's profits above a hurdle rate, on top of the management fee.
In many Cat I & II AIFs, the committed amount is drawn in stages over months or years, not invested upfront.
Private Placement Memorandum: the AIF's offer document with strategy, risks and full fee structure.
Early-stage and socially or economically desirable sectors.
Example: VC, SME, social impact, infrastructure, angel funds
Remember: Closed-ended; minimum 3-year tenure.
Everything not in Cat I or III; no leverage except temporary needs.
Example: Private equity, private credit, real estate
Remember: Closed-ended; minimum 3-year tenure.
Complex or trading strategies; may use leverage within limits.
Example: Long-short equity, hedge-style funds
Remember: Open- or closed-ended; generally taxed at fund level.
MF and AIF investors hold units of a pooled fund.
Example: PMS: securities in the client's own demat
Remember: Ownership drives visibility and tax.
MF: usually days. PMS: anytime, exit loads in years 1–3.
Example: Cat I & II AIF: typically locked 5–8+ years
Remember: Ask: "Can you leave this untouched for 5–7 years?"
MF: one SEBI-capped expense ratio in the NAV.
Example: PMS: fixed/profit share + brokerage, GST. AIF: management fee + carry
Remember: Always show costs in rupees, side by side.
MF: on redemption. PMS: every trade, client's hands.
Example: AIF Cat I & II: pass-through for most income; Cat III: fund level
Remember: Tax changes with Budgets; confirm with a CA.

Remember: Use the right yardstick and time frame.
Everyone, from the first rupee; emergency and short-term goals in liquid/debt funds.
Example: Salary earner starting a SIP
Remember: The core of every portfolio.
Surplus well above ₹50 lakh; wants own portfolio and full visibility.
Example: Investor with a solid MF core and tolerance for bigger swings
Remember: A satellite, never the whole portfolio.
₹1 crore+ that can be locked for years; wants private markets or complex strategies.

final.title: MF vs PMS vs AIF final quiz

questions.q: What is the SEBI minimum investment for a PMS?
questions.why: ₹50 lakh. The minimum was raised to ₹50 lakh in 2020.

questions.q: What is the minimum investment for an AIF for most investors?
questions.why: ₹1 crore. ₹25 lakh applies only to the manager's employees and directors.

questions.q: How many investors can an AIF scheme have at most?
questions.why: 1,000. AIF schemes are capped at 1,000 investors.

questions.q: Which AIF category includes venture capital and angel funds?
questions.why: Category I. Cat I covers early-stage and socially or economically desirable sectors.

questions.q: Which AIF category includes private equity and private credit funds?
questions.why: Category II. Cat II covers private-market funds.

questions.q: Which AIF category may use leverage and run long-short strategies?
questions.why: Category III. Cat III runs complex or trading strategies.

questions.q: What is the minimum tenure of a Category I or II AIF?
questions.why: 3 years. Both are closed-ended with at least 3 years.

questions.q: Where are the securities held in a PMS?
o: In the client's own demat account
questions.why: In the client's own demat account. This is why every trade is taxed in the client's hands.

questions.q: How can an AIF be marketed?
questions.why: Private placement only. Public invitation and mass marketing are not allowed.

questions.q: Which NISM certification is needed to distribute Category III AIFs?
questions.why: XIX-B. XIX-A is for Category I & II.

questions.q: How is distributor commission paid on Category III AIFs?
questions.why: Trail only. No upfront fee for Cat III; Cat I & II may pay up to one-third upfront.

questions.q: What is "carry" in an AIF?
o: The manager's share of profits above a hurdle
questions.why: The manager's share of profits above a hurdle. It is paid in addition to the management fee.

questions.q: What does the J-curve describe?
o: Early low or negative returns in PE/VC funds before exits
questions.why: Early low or negative returns in PE/VC funds before exits. Explain it before the client invests.

questions.q: What should every client have before adding PMS or AIF?
o: A diversified MF core and emergency fund
questions.why: A diversified MF core and emergency fund. Each rung of the ladder sits on the one below.

questions.q: What is the right yardstick for a Category II AIF?
o: IRR and multiple of money over the fund's life
questions.why: IRR and multiple of money over the fund's life. Judge over the full life of the fund.

questions.q: Do PMS and AIFs always deliver higher returns than mutual funds?
o: No — some do and some don't; compare after-fee returns and risk over a full cycle
questions.why: Some do and some don't; compare after-fee returns and risk over a full cycle.

questions.q: Can a client usually exit a Category II AIF whenever they like?
o: No — closed-ended; money returns as investments are exited
questions.why: Cat I & II are closed-ended; money returns as investments are exited.

questions.q: Category III AIFs are generally taxed:
o: In the investor's hands on every trade
Only on exit, at slab rate
questions.why: Cat I & II have pass-through status for most income.

questions.q: A client meets the ₹1 crore AIF minimum. Does that make them suitable?
o: No — eligible is not suitable; check lock-in tolerance and the core portfolio
Only if they already hold a PMS
questions.why: Eligible is not the same as suitable; check lock-in tolerance and the core portfolio.

questions.q: A social media post offers an “AIF with fixed 18% returns”. What is it?
o: A red flag: AIFs cannot be publicly advertised or promise returns
questions.why: AIFs cannot be publicly advertised or promise returns.

questions.q: A client asks, “What's the difference between MF, PMS and AIF?” Explain in under two minutes.
o: Minimum ticket (₹100s / ₹50 lakh / ₹1 crore), ownership (units vs own demat vs units), liquidity, costs and tax, in plain words
They are identical except for the name
questions.why: Covers minimum ticket (₹100s / ₹50 L / ₹1 Cr), ownership (units vs own demat vs units), liquidity, costs and tax, in plain words.

questions.q: A ₹60 lakh investor with no mutual fund core wants a PMS “because it's better”. How do you respond?
o: Eligible is not suitable; build the MF core and emergency fund first; PMS only later as a slice
Invest everything in the PMS now
questions.why: Eligible is not suitable; build the MF core and emergency fund first; PMS only later as a slice.

questions.q: A ₹5 crore client wants ₹2 crore in a private equity AIF but may need ₹50 lakh in two years for a house. What do you do?
o: Invest the full ₹2 crore including house money
Explain the lock-in and drawdowns; keep the house money liquid; size the AIF only from money not needed for years
Promise an exit in two years
Use the house money for the AIF
questions.why: Explains lock-in and capital calls; keeps the house money liquid; sizes the AIF only from money not needed for years.

questions.q: A client's VC AIF shows a negative return after 18 months and they want out. How do you respond?
o: Promise a recovery by next year
Explain the J-curve and closed-ended structure; review against the fund's plan; no promise of recovery
Arrange an immediate exit at full value
questions.why: Explains the J-curve and closed-ended structure; reviews against the fund's plan; no promise of recovery.

questions.q: A client asks why they should keep mutual funds now that they are “wealthy enough” for PMS and AIFs.
o: They shouldn't — drop all mutual funds
Liquidity, low cost, diversification and tax efficiency of the MF core; the ladder adds, it doesn't replace
Mutual funds are only for small investors
Move everything to a Category III AIF
questions.why: Liquidity, low cost, diversification and tax efficiency of the MF core; the ladder adds, it doesn't replace.
